findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR is titled 'Advanced Query Processing Architecture' but the entire diff is a ~10-line change to when/where Loki template-variable interpolation runs inside the two split-query entry points; no work in the diff is traceable to any architectural deliverable. Reviewers and changelog consumers cannot map the stated scope to the shipped change; if 'Advanced Query Processing Architecture' was the intended scope, the required work is missing and this PR under-delivers under a title that overstates it, so scope gets silently redefined at merge time.

[ADVISORY] runShardSplitQuery now runs each query through datasource.applyTemplateVariables and the downstream shard-group construction runs the same queries through it again — the diff's own updated test asserts applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times for a single input query ('expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)'). Template interpolation, including adhoc-filter injection into the stream selector, is applied multiple times to the same expr; correctness now silently depends on applyTemplateVariables being idempotent, and any non-idempotent variable format (e.g. regex/quoting formats applied to already-transformed values) produces corrupted expressions, with the per-shard-group re-interpolation also adding work proportional to shard-group count on every request.

[ADVISORY] runSplitQuery now applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) to every filtered target, including the nonSplittingQueries partition that the splitting feature merely forwards to runQuery — expanding the split runner's responsibility beyond splitting into owning interpolation for queries it does not split. Template-variable and adhoc-filter application for non-splitting queries now lives in two layers (this map and the datasource's own query path); nothing in the diff enforces an invariant that a query is interpolated exactly once, so any path where both layers process the same targets double-applies interpolation or injects adhoc filters twice, and no test in the diff covers the non-splitting-query branch of this new map call.

[BUG] runSplitQuery now interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables, but those interpolated targets are then handed to datasource.runQuery and on to LokiDatasource.query(), which runs applyTemplateVariables on them again — every split query is now interpolated twice. The happy-path tests only use idempotent replacements ('$__auto' -> '5m'), which hide the regression: any variable whose interpolated value contains a '$' character or regex-format escaping (e.g. a regex variable value 'foo\.bar') is re-processed by the second pass, double-escaping the value or re-interpolating embedded '$' tokens and sending a corrupted LogQL expression to Loki — only on split-query paths. It also applies ad-hoc filters (request.filters) a second time downstream, duplicating matchers in the stream selector.

[BUG] The refactor from interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, request.scopedVars) to per-query datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) silently adds ad-hoc filters to the shard-splitting path, which the removed call never passed. When a dashboard has ad-hoc filters, they are now baked into the expr before splitQueriesByStreamShard runs, so the stream selector sent to languageProvider.fetchLabelValues and the resulting shard grouping change versus the previous behavior — and the filters are applied a second time downstream by datasource.query(), producing selectors with duplicated matchers. This is an objective change buried in what reads as a mechanical API swap, with no test in the diff passing request.filters to confirm the new behavior is intended.

[ADVISORY] The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' tests (here and in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts) stub applyTemplateVariables with a single-argument mock that ignores scopedVars/filters and mock datasource.runQuery entirely, so no test exercises the second, downstream interpolation/application pass that the diff's changes interact with. The exact regression surfaces this diff opens — double interpolation of '$'-containing values and double application of ad-hoc filters — cannot fail these tests: a future change that makes the double pass corrupt queries ships green. The shard-path test mocks (shardQuerySplitting.test.ts lines 56-58, 173-175) likewise accept only (query), so filter handling introduced by the new third argument is entirely untested.

[BUG] The new .map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)) runs BEFORE the partition through querySupportsSplitting(query), so the $__auto token that query splitting keys on is replaced with a concrete interval (e.g. '5m') before the split/no-split decision is made, degrading $__auto queries to the non-splitting path. A $__auto range query over a multi-day window is executed as a single unsplit request instead of being chunked, producing Loki timeouts/OOM-style failures and full-range scans that splitting was built to avoid. The new test 'Interpolates queries before execution' (querySplitting.test.ts:75-89) cannot detect this: it asserts only the expr and step of mock.calls[0][0].targets[0], which are identical whether the query was split into multiple chunk requests or executed whole — it never asserts the number of runQuery calls or the per-chunk ranges (unlike the pre-existing tests such as 'Skips partial updates as an option' which assert '3 days, 3 chunks, 3 requests'). I checked querySplitting.test.ts and shardQuerySplitting.test.ts in this diff; no test in the diff asserts that a query containing $__auto still produces multiple chunked requests after the interpolation was moved ahead of the partition.

[BUG] The reorder from 'interpolate then filter by expr' to 'filter by expr then interpolate' drops the old guarantee that queries whose expr consists solely of a template variable that resolves to an empty string are excluded, because '$var' is truthy before interpolation. A panel target with expr '$expr' where the variable is unset now survives the .filter((query) => query.expr) gate (previously interpolateVariablesInQueries ran on all targets first and the empty result was filtered out) and flows into splitQueriesByStreamShard, which fetches label values for an empty selector and executes requests with an empty expr, surfacing Loki request errors to the user instead of silently dropping the target. I checked shardQuerySplitting.test.ts and querySplitting.test.ts in this diff: every test uses a concrete expr or a variable that interpolates to a non-empty selector; no test exercises an expr that interpolates to empty.

[ADVISORY] The updated assertion expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5) is an implementation-coupled call count that silently encodes redundant re-application of applyTemplateVariables: the request contains a single target, so 5 calls means 1 call from the new map in runShardSplitQuery plus 4 calls on already-interpolated shard-group queries derived from it inside splitQueriesByStreamShard. Maintainers get a test that asserts call mechanics rather than interpolation semantics — any change to shard grouping (e.g. different group count for the ['1','10','2','20','3'] fixture) breaks this test spuriously, while a genuine double-interpolation defect (a variable value containing '$' being mangled on the second pass) would still pass since the test only counts calls. The behavioral counterpart in the new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test covers the final expr, making the count assertion redundant weight that must be hand-updated on every internal refactor.

[ADVISORY] The source change adds a new third argument request.filters to the applyTemplateVariables call in both querySplitting.ts:297 and shardQuerySplitting.ts:52, but no test in the diff asserts that adhoc filters are actually forwarded and applied — the new querySplitting test's replace implementation ignores everything except $__auto/$step, and the shard tests' mock has signature (query: LokiQuery) that discards the scopedVars and filters arguments entirely. If a regression stops request.filters from reaching applyTemplateVariables (e.g. a refactor back to the two-argument call, which is exactly the shape the shard test mock invites since its implementation only reads the first parameter), the 'Interpolates queries before execution' tests still pass while adhoc dashboard filters silently stop being applied to split queries, returning unfiltered results to users. I checked querySplitting.test.ts and shardQuerySplitting.test.ts; no assertion inspects the second or third arguments passed to applyTemplateVariables.

goldens.comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

The diff doesn’t prove a concrete correctness failure, but it does establish repeated interpolation and therefore a real risk/perf concern: behavior now implicitly relies on `applyTemplateVariables` being idempotent and adds work proportional to shard/group count.

The claim of "interpolated twice" and duplicated matchers depends on behavior outside this diff, so it isn’t verifiable from the provided changes alone.

This reordering could affect the splitting decision if `querySupportsSplitting` depends on unexpanded tokens (the finding’s specific claim about `$__auto` cannot be verified from this diff because `querySupportsSplitting` is not shown). adjudication.rationale: In both `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery`, targets are now filtered with `.filter((query) => query.expr)` *before* interpolation via `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))`. Previously (at least in `runShardSplitQuery`), interpolation happened first (`interpolateVariablesInQueries(...)`) and only then did the code filter by `expr`. With the new order, a target like `expr: '$var'` will pass the pre-interpolation truthy check, but may become an empty string after `applyTemplateVariables`, and there is no subsequent `expr` filter to drop it before calling `splitQueriesByStreamShard` / proceeding to execution. The added tests only cover interpolation to non-empty strings and do not cover the empty-interpolation case.

Asserting an exact total call count is therefore tightly coupled to internal mechanics (number of derived queries/groups), making the test fragile to refactors or shard grouping changes, while the newly added "Interpolates queries before execution" test already asserts the interpolated `expr`/`step` semantics.
